---
title: Detectors and triggers
guide-section: How it works
---

## Detectors

A detector is anything with two methods (`detectors.Detector`):

- `read()` returns a `Reading(level, rising)`. Either may be `None` when unknown.
- `listen(callback)` calls `callback` whenever the level may have changed.

`SunDetector` reads the `elevation` and `rising` attributes of `sun.sun` and listens for changes to `elevation`.

In `apps.yaml` a detector is a mapping with a `kind`, parsed by `detectors.DetectorConfig`:

```yaml
detector:
  kind: sun
```

Each config model has a `build(app)` method that returns its detector.

## Triggers

A trigger has a `listen(app, callback)` method (`triggers.Trigger`). Triggers in `start` are parsed by `triggers.TriggerConfig`:

| model | yaml | fires |
|---|---|---|
| `Daily` | `- daily: "05:45:00"` | daily at that time, via AppDaemon `run_daily` |
| `Event` | `- event: bedroom_alarm` | when the Home Assistant event fires, via `listen_event` |

`LightFadeApp` always adds an `Event` trigger for `<app name>` plus `EVENT_SUFFIX`, the test event. Every trigger calls `LightFade.start()`.

## Lights

`lights.Light` is what a fade writes to: `brightness_pct()`, `turn_on(pct, transition)` and `turn_off(transition)`. `HassLight` implements it with the `light.turn_on` and `light.turn_off` services.
